subsystems.name: Electrode array
subsystems.role: picks up microvolt-scale voltages from the scalp through hair without conductive gel.

subsystems.name: Analog front end
subsystems.role: amplifies tiny signals while rejecting noise.

subsystems.name: Digitisation and link
subsystems.role: converts the analog signal to digital data and streams it wirelessly.

subsystems.name: Signal processing
subsystems.role: cleans the data and extracts features.

subsystems.name: Decoding model
subsystems.role: maps brain patterns to commands, attention scores or text.

subsystems.name: Application layer
subsystems.role: turns decoded output into something useful.

buildSteps.title: Choose the paradigm
buildSteps.detail: Decide whether the system uses motor imagery, steady-state visual evoked potentials, or attention-related rhythms, because each dictates electrode placement.

buildSteps.title: Design the headband
buildSteps.detail: A flexible frame is shaped to hold electrodes at standard scalp positions (the 10–20 system) and to stay put during head movement.

buildSteps.title: Build the electrodes
buildSteps.detail: Conductive elastomer or metal pins are made to contact the scalp through hair with low and stable impedance.

buildSteps.title: Assemble the electronics
buildSteps.detail: The analog front end is laid out to keep noise below a microvolt, then shielded from the radio and power supply.

buildSteps.title: Calibrate and collect data
buildSteps.detail: Each user performs guided tasks while labelled brain data is recorded; the model is trained or fine-tuned on those labels.

buildSteps.title: Validate
buildSteps.detail: Performance is tested against chance and against conventional input, with false-positive and fatigue rates measured.

buildSteps.title: Integrate and ship
buildSteps.detail: The decoder is embedded in software or firmware, with limits on what data leaves the device.

prerequisites.why: gel-free contact through hair is less stable than laboratory gel electrodes, so signals drift.
brain signals are only a few microvolts and are easily drowned by mains hum and muscle activity.
models must generalise across users and sessions; most still need per-person calibration.
decoding improves with data, but privacy and variability make such datasets scarce.
signals degrade as the headband slips or the user tires.

pathway.milestone: consumer headsets that report coarse attention or relaxation, and research spellers using P300 or SSVEP
pathway.unlocks: real but low-bandwidth control, mainly for accessibility and focus tracking.

pathway.milestone: calibration-free decoders that work across users and sessions
pathway.unlocks: a device you can put on and use immediately, like a mouse.

pathway.milestone: dry sensors with signal quality approaching gel electrodes
pathway.unlocks: reliable control without a technician or conductive paste.

pathway.milestone: high-bandwidth non-invasive decoding of imagined speech or movement
pathway.unlocks: typing and device control at useful speeds for people with severe paralysis — though skull and tissue blur the signal, so invasive arrays will likely stay ahead for the hardest cases.
